 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1.
These are petitions seeking bail by four brothers in respect of FIR no.83/22 dated 09.04.2022.

2. We have heard Shri Siddharth Luthra and Shri Siddharth Bhatnagar, learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners and Smt. Garima Prasad, learned Additional Advocate General for the respondent/State.

3. It is the submission of the learned senior counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in the cases since the father of the petitioner was a Member of Legislative Council belonging to a political party.

It is submitted that the modus operandi that is operated by the State is that when the petitioners get bail in one matter, another FIR is lodged against them so as to ensure that they never get the benefit of the bail orders.

It is further submitted that in most of the cases,
which have been relied on by the State to oppose the case on the ground of criminal antecedents,

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: either the petitioners have been acquitted or released on bail.
It is submitted that in four cases this Court has quashed the proceedings in respect of some of the petitioners.
4. Ms. Garima Prasad, learned senior counsel, vehemently opposed the petitions.
She submits that the petitioners are involved in as many as 28 cases.
She further submits that some of the cases even pertain to gang rape.
It is therefore submitted that the petitioners are not entitled to be released on bail.
She further submits that the provisions in Section 19(4) of the Gangsters Act are akin to Section 37 of the Nacrotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and Section 45 of the PMLA.

entities.text: Nacrotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: She therefore submits that unless the Court comes to a finding that the accused are not involved in the offence and that they are not likely to commit the offence if they are released on bail, the Court cannot consider their application for bail.
Ms. Prasad, further submits that the father of the petitioners has fled away from the country and there is every possibility that the petitioners may also flee away.
5. We have perused the material on record.
No doubt that the chart in the counter affidavit shows that the petitioners are involved in 28 cases.
However, it is to be seen that in most of the cases, the petitioners have either been released on bail or acquitted and in some cases this Court has quashed the proceedings against the petitioners.

Insofar as the serious offence with regard to the gang rape is concerned, the perusal of the order passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Saharanpur dated 11.07.2022 in Bail Application No.3110/2022 would reveal that the petitioners have also been released on bail in the said matter by a detailed order.

6. It could thus be seen that though the petitioners were involved in a serious offence like Section 376 of the IPC and Sections 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and that though they have been released on bail vide order dated 11.07.2022, no steps are taken for cancellation of the said bail order even after a period of two and a half years has lapsed therefrom.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
7. Insofar as the contention of the petitioners with regard to sub-section (4) of Section 19 of the Gangsters Act is concerned, this Court in the case of Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement,
2024 INSC 595, has held that statutory restrictions cannot override the constitutional guarantees, as provided under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

entities.text:
Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement,
2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been held that a prolonged incarceration cannot be permitted to be turned into sentence without trial.
In the present case, there is no likelihood of the trial being concluded in the near future.
We are therefore, inclined to allow the petitions.
8. Insofar as the apprehension of the respondent/State regarding fleeing away of the petitioners is concerned, we are informed that their passports are also impounded.
As such there is no possibility of the petitioners fleeing away.
9. It is further directed that the petitioners shall regularly attend the proceedings before the Trial Court and cooperate in the expeditious conclusion of trial.
10. The petitioners are directed to be released on bail in connection with Sessions Trial No.648 of 2023 arising out of FIR No.83/22 dated 09.04.2022, to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
